chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a wet mouse that fell into water and walked on the clothes upon which one prays. He said: 'Wash what you see of its trace, and sprinkle with water what you do not see.'
ai.seo_question: How to purify clothes contaminated by a wet mouse according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the prominent Ja'fari lineage of Imam Musa al-Kadhim, this hadith clarifies the distinction between major impurity (najis) and minor impurity in practical jurisprudence. It establishes that visible traces of a wet mouse necessitate full washing (ghasl), while invisible traces are purified through mere sprinkling (in'dih), reflecting the Shia principle of caution in ritual purity.
